title: Identification of NF-kappaB pathway-related biomarkers in myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury: based on transcriptomics analysis and RT-qPCR validation.
authors: Ting, Wang; Helong, Xiao; Xiaoyu, Wang; Chuanqiang, Wang; Xiao, Hu; Yang, Yang; Zhe, Yuan; Shaopeng, Xu; Xiaoyong, Geng
one_liner_zh: 该研究基于转录组学和RT-qPCR鉴定心肌缺血再灌注损伤中NF-kappaB通路相关生物标志物，虽涉及转录因子网络和分子对接，但核心是疾病标志物发现而非蛋白质-DNA互作机制建模，方法以常规生信和湿实验为主，与课题关联较弱。
abstract: Myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury (MIRI) limits the success of reperfusion therapies. Identifying potential biomarkers within the nuclear factor kappa-B (NF-kappaB) pathway is critical for developing new treatments. Transcriptomic data from mouse MIRI models were combined with NF-kappaB pathway-related genes. Candidate genes were identified from the overlapping differentially expressed genes. Potential biomarkers were selected via protein-protein interaction network analysis and validated with independent datasets. We performed functional analysis, built transcription factor and competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA) networks, and conducted drug prediction and molecular docking. Reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) validation was performed in a MIRI mouse model. Nine candidate genes were identified, with Nfkbia and Icam1 emerging as potential biomarkers. Functional analysis connected Nfkbia to mitochondrial metabolism and Icam1 to extracellular matrix processes/nuclear processes. A regulatory network involving mmu-miR-706 and seven lncRNAs was constructed. Drug prediction identified Tosyllysyl Chloromethyl Ketone (TLCK) as exhibiting favourable binding affinity for both targets. Experimental validation confirmed significant upregulation of Nfkbia and Icam1 in MIRI. This study established Nfkbia and Icam1 as key NF-kappaB-associated genes in MIRI and constructed a ceRNA network. These findings advance our understanding of MIRI mechanisms and support future therapy development. However, these findings were based on bioinformatics analysis and preliminary experimental validation, and required further functional experiments for confirmation.
abstract_zh: 心肌缺血再灌注损伤（MIRI）限制了再灌注治疗的成功。识别核因子kappa-B（NF-kappaB）通路中的潜在生物标志物对于开发新疗法至关重要。将小鼠MIRI模型的转录组数据与NF-kappaB通路相关基因相结合。从重叠的差异表达基因中鉴定候选基因。通过蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用网络分析筛选潜在生物标志物，并使用独立数据集进行验证。我们进行了功能分析，构建了转录因子和竞争性内源RNA（ceRNA）网络，并进行了药物预测和分子对接。在MIRI小鼠模型中进行了逆转录定量聚合酶链反应（RT-qPCR）验证。鉴定出九个候选基因，其中Nfkbia和Icam1成为潜在生物标志物。功能分析将Nfkbia与线粒体代谢相关联，将Icam1与细胞外基质过程/核过程相关联。构建了涉及mmu-miR-706和七个长链非编码RNA（lncRNAs）的调控网络。药物预测确定甲苯磺酰赖氨酰氯甲基酮（TLCK）对两个靶点均表现出良好的结合亲和力。实验验证确认Nfkbia和Icam1在MIRI中显著上调。本研究确立了Nfkbia和Icam1作为MIRI中关键的NF-kappaB相关基因，并构建了ceRNA网络。这些发现增进了我们对MIRI机制的理解，并支持未来疗法的开发。然而，这些发现基于生物信息学分析和初步实验验证，仍需进一步的功能实验加以确认。
